products.name: Remote Help for the Enterprise Help Desk — Operations, Unattended Access & Adoption at Scale — Commercial
products.short_description: Take Remote Help from 'installed' to a running help-desk capability — role design, unattended access, escalation workflow, usage reporting, and end-user adoption at scale.
products.description:
Take Remote Help from 'installed' to a running help-desk capability — role design, unattended access, escalation workflow, usage reporting, and end-user adoption at scale.

Deploying Remote Help is the easy part; running it as a help-desk capability is where value is won or lost. Once the app is in place, an enterprise still needs the operating model: who can help whom (RBAC roles and scope), when unattended access is appropriate and how it's governed, how a session fits the ticket/escalation workflow, how usage and outcomes are measured, and how end users learn to trust and request it. This solution is that operations-and-adoption layer on top of a Remote Help deployment — it assumes the app is (or will be) deployed and does NOT re-teach base setup; it builds the help-desk practice around it.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Role & scope design — map help-desk tiers to Remote Help RBAC roles and scope so agents can help exactly the users they should, and no more
  • Attended vs unattended access — when unattended is appropriate, how it's governed and consented, and the guardrails around it (flagged verify-with-Microsoft for current capability)
  • Help-desk workflow — fit a Remote Help session into ticket intake, verification, escalation tiers, and session logging/handoff
  • Measure it — usage, session outcomes, and adoption reporting; define the KPIs that show the capability is working
  • Drive adoption — end-user comms, how to request help, trust/consent expectations, and an agent enablement plan

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Remote Help running as a real help-desk capability — right-scoped roles, governed unattended access, a session-to-ticket workflow, outcome reporting, and adoption — not just an installed app.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • RHELPOPS-Discovery.ps1 — read-only discovery of the Remote Help help-desk operating model (Graph)
    • RHELPOPS-Report.ps1 — export Remote Help usage / outcome / adoption KPIs to CSV (Graph)
    • RHELPOPS-Set-RoleScope.ps1 — assign a Remote Help RBAC role + scope group to a help-desk tier (Graph)
    • RHELPOPS-Test-Scope.ps1 — prove a help-desk tier is scoped to the intended users and no more (Graph)
    • RHELPOPS-Validate.ps1 — PASS/FAIL validation of the Remote Help operating model (Graph)

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
